q-0327.answer:
Surah Al-A'raaf (7) — The Heights · 206 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Do not disregard what the Messenger ﷺ brought you and follow something else, for in this case, you will be deviating from Allah's judgment to the decision of someone else.
• We destroyed what Fir'awn and his people produced, such as agriculture and buildings.
• Remember your Lord in secret, not loudly, with eagerness and fear.
• Follow and imitate the unlettered Prophet ﷺ, who brought you a Book that was revealed for you, from the Lord and master of everything.
• Having doubt about it according to Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0455.answer:
Surah Az-Zumar (39) — The Groups · 75 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• He will not accept any deed unless it is done purely and sincerely for Him Alone, with no partner or associate.
• Allah is Sufficient for His Servant
• The matter is not as he claims; on the contrary, We have blessed him with this as a test to see whether he will be obedient or disobedient – although We have prior knowledge of that.
• All of creation, whether animate or inanimate, will speak words of praise to Allah, the Lord of all that exists, for His wisdom and justice.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

Surah Al-Waaqia (56) — The Inevitable · 96 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Relentlessly pulverized. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah and others.
• We caused the seeds to grow with Our compassion and mercy and left them intact inside the earth as mercy for you.
• The angels will deliver the good news to them by saying, "Peace be upon you," i.
• It is shaken and moved violently over all of its surface and through its depths.

q-0594.answer: Scholars classify the 114 surahs by where they were first revealed: approximately **86 surahs are Meccan** (revealed before Hijrah in Makkah) and **28 are Medinan** (revealed after Hijrah in Madinah). Meccan surahs often focus on faith, tawhid, and the Hereafter; Medinan surahs often address law, community, and governance. Individual surah pages show each surah's revelation type.

Surah Al-Burooj (85) — The Constellations · 22 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• The Explanation of the Promised Day and the Witness and the Witnessed
• Indeed His punishment and His vengeance upon His enemies, who have rejected His Messengers, and opposed His command, is severe, great and strong.
• The Oppression of the People of the Ditch against the Muslims
• When He seizes the wrongdoer, He seizes him with a severe and painful punishment.
• They did not commit any sin according to these people, except for their faith in Allah the Almighty, Who does not treat unjustly those who desire to be with Him.

q-0712.answer:
Surah Al-Humaza (104) — The Traducer · 9 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• The person who gathered wealth and counted it, will be thrown into Al-Hutamah, which is one of the descriptive names of the Hellfire.
• He gathers it piling some of it on top of the rest and he counts it up.
• Woe to every scorner and mocker
• Who collects wealth and [continuously] counts it.
• He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal.

Transliteration: Yaaa aiyuhal lazeena aamanoo laa tuhilloo sha'aaa 'iral laahi wa lash Shahral Haraama wa lal hadya wa lal qalaaa'ida wa laa aaammeenal Baital Haraama yabtaghoona fadlam mir Rabbihim wa ridwaanaa; wa izaa halaltum fastaadoo; wa laa yajrimannakum shana aanu qawmin an saddookum 'anil Masjidil-Haraami an ta'tadoo; wa ta'aawanoo 'alalbirri wattaqwaa; wa laa ta'aawanoo 'alal ismi wal'udwaan; wattaqul laah; innal laaha shadeedul 'iqaab

Translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or [the sanctity of] the sacred month or [neglect the marking of] the sacrificial animals and garlanding [them] or [violate the safety of] those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. But when you come out of ihram, then [you may] hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.

Translation: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and fought with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah and those who gave shelter and aided - they are allies of one another. c-0040.answer:
Two verses draw the attention. "Do the disbelievers not see that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, then We parted them — and We made from water every living thing?" (21:30). And: "We built the heaven with power, and indeed We are expanding it" (51:47) — the participle musi'un carrying the sense of continually extending, a reading classical dictionaries support and which sits remarkably beside the discovery (1929) that space itself expands.

The honest framing matters. Muslims do not claim the Quran is a physics paper, and responsible scholars warn against chaining tafsir to any era's provisional science. The claim is more modest and more interesting: a 7th-century text addressing all of history had endless opportunities to enshrine the cosmologies of its day — a static cosmos, crystalline spheres, a flat disc — and instead speaks of an initial unity parted, an ongoing expansion, orbits in which sun and moon swim (36:40), and a universe created "in truth and for an appointed term" (46:3), i.e., with a beginning and an end. Nothing there has needed retraction in fourteen centuries — which is precisely the pattern you'd expect from the verse's own challenge: "Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction" (4:82).
